interpretations: "Wins in the standings at each race" means driverStandings.wins, a running season-to-date count, and each race's figure is the average of that count over all drivers with standings rows at that race. The country figure is the plain average of those race figures. The overall average is the unweighted mean of the country averages. The above-average group is the countries above that mean. The final list is the countries in that group above the group's mean
Same as 1, but each race's figure is the sum of all drivers' standings wins at that race, not the average. The country figure is then the average of those sums
Same as 1, but each race's figure is the maximum standings wins at that race, which is the leader's win count. The country figure is the average of those maxima
Same as 1, but the race figure averages only drivers with at least one win, or only drivers who finished the race (those with results)
Same as 1, but the overall average is weighted by race count. It is the average across all races at all circuits in all countries, not the mean of the country averages
Same as 1, but the group average is weighted by race count within the above-average group, not the mean of the group's country averages
Same as 1, but "above the average across countries" is judged against the average of all race-level figures pooled together. The group average is the mean of the above-average countries' averages
"Wins" means each driver's wins from the results table (positionOrder = 1) or the constructorStandings wins, not driverStandings.wins. Everything else follows
"Wins" means per-race wins. This is the change in the running count from the previous race, or 1 if the driver won that race. The aggregation is otherwise as in
"Above the average" is read as greater than or equal to the average, so countries exactly at the average are included

The output is read as: country, average wins, difference from the overall average (average minus overall average), and difference from the group average (average minus group average). The differences might instead be reported as percentages above each average
The second filter might be applied to all countries (above the group average), not only to those in the above-average group. In practice this gives the same set

Countries are grouped by circuits.country, joined through races.circuitId. Alternatively, "country" might be read as the driver's nationality or the constructor's nationality, though "circuit country" fixes it as the circuit's country
Races with no standings rows are either excluded from the country's race count, or counted as zero wins in the country average
Averaging across a country's races is done per race (each raceId counted once), or per circuit first (averaging across circuits in the country, then across the country)
Averaging across all seasons, or limited to a single year
The results are ordered by average wins descending, or left unordered
Missing interpretations:
"Wins in the standings at each race" uses only the final standings row per driver per season, or the end-of-season value, rather than the running value at every race
"Wins" is the per-driver season total (maximum wins in the season), averaged by country without first averaging per race
The country figure is the average of all driver standings rows at the country's races, pooled (row-weighted), not the average of race-level averages

The overall average across countries is computed over all countries, but the above-average group is determined with a strict comparison. The group average includes ties and uses a different rounding or precision
"Drivers' wins" is limited to drivers who actually raced (those with results rows at that race). Interpretation 4 mentions this only as an alternative, not as a separate reading
The "how far above" differences are reported as ratios or multiples (average divided by the average), not as absolute or percentage differences
Circuits with null or empty countries are excluded or treated as their own group
queries:
WITH race_avg AS (
  SELECT raceId, AVG(wins) AS w
  FROM driverStandings
  GROUP BY raceId
),
country_avg AS (
  SELECT c.country AS country, AVG(r.w) AS avg_w
  FROM race_avg r
  JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId
  JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = ra.circuitId
  GROUP BY c.country
),
above AS (
  SELECT country, avg_w
  FROM country_avg
  WHERE avg_w > (SELECT AVG(avg_w) FROM country_avg)
)
SELECT country
FROM above
WHERE avg_w > (SELECT AVG(avg_w) FROM above);
SELECT c.country, AVG(r.race_wins) AS avg_wins
FROM (
  SELECT ra.raceId, ra.circuitId, SUM(ds.wins) AS race_wins
  FROM races ra
  JOIN driverStandings ds ON ds.raceId = ra.raceId
  GROUP BY ra.raceId, ra.circuitId
) r
JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
GROUP BY c.country;
SELECT c.country, AVG(m.max_wins) AS avg_max_wins
FROM (
  SELECT raceId, MAX(wins) AS max_wins
  FROM driverStandings
  GROUP BY raceId
) m
JOIN races r ON r.raceId = m.raceId
JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
GROUP BY c.country;
